newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt mostly unchanged in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt mostly unchanged in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds barely budged on Friday as market participants kept to the sidelines ahead of key U.S. economic data due out next week, investment-grade bond traders said.

"I would tend to think that people are looking for validation so economic news next week certainly has the potential to potentially swing the market. Is it enough to keep out of it? I would have to think so," said one investment-grade bond trader.
Key data includes February's NAPM report due out on Monday and the February employment report on Friday.
Another key factor that may keep investors sidelined is testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to the U.S. House banking committee on Wednesday.

In the secondary corporate bond market, sources said MFS Communications 8-7/8 percent senior discount notes and its 9-3/8 percent senior discount notes ended the day 1/2 higher at 76-3/4 and 89-3/4, respectively.
One market source said MFS'S favorable earnings report and expectations of an upgrade by Moody's Investors Service IN and Standard and Poor's Corp helped bolster prices.
In the broader market, sources said prices were unchanged.
"It was really quiet here. We didn't see much action today. Greenspan's comments earlier this week I think had everyone frozen in their tracks," said one corporate trader.

"I don't think the market was in a position to cause people to have some real conviction. It wasn't cheap enough to buy and it wasn't rich enough to sell and after Greenspan's comments it changed the whole ball game."
In the high-yield corporate bond market, Revlon Worldwide Corp's zero coupon bonds ended the day unchanged at about 65-5/8 after falling 1/8 when it intitially freed syndicate.
Revlon, which was lead managed by Chase Securities, priced $500 million of 144A zero coupon senior discount notes due March 15, 2001 at 65.59 to yield 10-3/4 percent.
Elsewhere, Mapco Inc issued a $200 million two-tranche offering via co-lead managers J.P. Morgan Securities Inc and Chase Securities.

The first tranche totalled $100 million of 7-1/4 percent notes due 2009 at 99.76 to yield 7.28 percent and the second tranche comprised $100 million 7.70 percent bonds due 2027 at 99.677 to yield 7.728 percent.
Lastly, Tracor Inc issued $250 million 10-year 8-1/2 percent notes at 99.602 to yield 8.56 percent or 200 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
The deal, which was lead managed by BT Securities, was increased in from its original amount of $50 million.
Looking ahead, sources said they expect few new borrowings by U.S. corporation until the Greenspan testimony and the U.S. economic reports were out of the way.

"I don't think there is any borrowing that absolutely has to get done. If somebody feels absolutely compelled they will obviously push it but I think for the most part it is discretionary borrowing and I think they will wait for more friendly market conditions," the source said.
